key_insight: GRPO’s U-statistic structure turns group-size selection from trial and error into a variance-ratio estimation problem.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive group sizes can improve policy-gradient accuracy and reasoning-model training with modest additional computational cost.
method: Express GRPO’s policy gradient using U-statistics to guide group-size selection.
Use a pessimistic ratio estimator that accounts for uncertainty in a potentially small denominator.
Analyze three sample-size regimes and implement a jackknife-based selection rule.
evidence_signal: Experiments on synthetic Reasoning Gym tasks and real-world math and code benchmarks report lower policy-gradient mean squared error and better policy optimization than fixed-group-size baselines.
watch_item: Near-zero variance-ratio denominators make estimation delicate; the abstract does not quantify gains or computational overhead.
